info.title: Sysnet API
info.description:
## Authorization
We use bearer auth throughout the API. Generally, API requests should have the follow header:  
{  
    "content-type": "application/json",  
    "Authorization": "Bearer TOKEN_GOES_HERE"  
}  
Please refer to the Auth section immediately below for details on getting your token.

get.description:
Search for AuditLog objects

AuditLogs store information about insert, updates, patches and deletes. So that all user actions can be traced.

You will need to have the following data accesses assigned to your user to use this route: sc_get_auditlogs

parameters.name: view
parameters.description:
The view is the list of fields you want returned.

### View Templates
FKExternalKeys

 - **VenueIdFKObject:** venueId, externalKeys

parameters.name: group
parameters.description:
This parameter is used to group results.
                        The fieldName can be any of the following: venueId.
                        The sort could either have - to sort by descending and + to sort by ascending. See groupQuery schema for more info.
                        For grouping using a nested field use <object>.<field> to specify the nested levels eg +Stock.name

parameters.name: groupSummary
parameters.description:
This parameter is used to summarise grouped results by aggregating the groups.
                The fieldName can be any of the following: auditLogId.
                        The type could be count,min,max,sum,avg. See groupSummaryQuery schema for more info.

parameters.name: totalSummary
parameters.description:
This parameter is used to summarise all grouped results by aggregating all the groups sub groups.
                The fieldName can be any of the following: auditLogId.
                        The type could be count,min,max,sum,avg. See groupSummaryQuery schema for more info.

parameters.name: searchDistinct
parameters.description:
This parameter is used to get the distinct values for a field. 
                Only the field specified will be returned in the results. This can be used with filtering functionality, sort and limit. 
                However it cannot be used with group, groupSummary or totalSummary.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
This parameter is used to change the sorting of results returned. 
                        The default sort is auditLogId ascending. 
                        Use any fieldNames comma separated in the sort. 
                        Use + for ascending - for descending 
                        eg +updateDateTime.
                        - auditLogId would sort by updateDateTime ascending and then auditLogId descending.
 For sorting using a nested field use <object>.<field> to specify the nested levels eg +Stock.name
                        For sorting using a nested field use <object>.<field> to specify the nested levels eg +Stock.name

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: This limits the amount of results returned. This default limit Is set to 20. The maximum limit is 200.

parameters.name: auditLogId
parameters.description:
The unique primary Key, used to identify a record
integer: This parameter searches the auditLogId field and returns all available results that match. You can use >10 to search for all auditLogIds greater than 10. You can use [1,2,3] to search for auditLogIds that match either 1, 2 or 3. You can use this parameter multiple times. eg auditLogId=>5& auditLogId=<10 would search for all auditLogIds between 5 and 10.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: This parameter searches for the message field and returns all available results that match. You can use this parameter multiple times and it will do an 'AND' search. You can use * as a wildcard. You can use brackets and a comma to perform an ‘OR’ search e.g [a,b*] will search for ‘a’ OR a value starting with ‘b’.

parameters.name: loggedInUserId
parameters.description: This parameter searches for the loggedInUserId field and returns all available results that match. You can use this parameter multiple times and it will do an 'AND' search. You can use * as a wildcard. You can use brackets and a comma to perform an ‘OR’ search e.g [a,b*] will search for ‘a’ OR a value starting with ‘b’.

parameters.name: tableName
parameters.description:
This is the table/object affected. Example Value: Items
This parameter searches for the tableName field and returns all available results that match. You can use this parameter multiple times and it will do an 'AND' search. You can use * as a wildcard. You can use brackets and a comma to perform an ‘OR’ search e.g [a,b*] will search for ‘a’ OR a value starting with ‘b’.

parameters.name: tableId
parameters.description: This parameter searches for the tableId field and returns all available results that match. You can use this parameter multiple times and it will do an 'AND' search. You can use * as a wildcard. You can use brackets and a comma to perform an ‘OR’ search e.g [a,b*] will search for ‘a’ OR a value starting with ‘b’.

parameters.name: ipAddress
parameters.description: This parameter searches for the ipAddress field and returns all available results that match. You can use this parameter multiple times and it will do an 'AND' search. You can use * as a wildcard. You can use brackets and a comma to perform an ‘OR’ search e.g [a,b*] will search for ‘a’ OR a value starting with ‘b’.

parameters.name: details
parameters.description:
In the case of an update, insert or patches this field contains the HTTP body of the request. For deletes, this field contains the deleted object.
This parameter searches for the details field and returns all available results that match. You can use this parameter multiple times and it will do an 'AND' search. You can use * as a wildcard. You can use brackets and a comma to perform an ‘OR’ search e.g [a,b*] will search for ‘a’ OR a value starting with ‘b’.

parameters.name: logDate
parameters.description: string: This parameter searches the logDate field and returns all available results that match. You can use >12 jan 2020 5:30:20 GMT+10:30 to search for all logDates greater than 12 jan 2020 5:30:20 GMT+10:30. You can use [1,2,3] to search for logDates that match either 1, 2 or 3. You can use this parameter multiple times. eg logDate=>12 jan 2020 5:30:20 GMT+10:30& logDate=<12 jan 2020 5:30:20 GMT+10:30 would search for all logDates between 12 jan 2020 5:30:20 GMT+10:30 and 14 jan 2020 5:30:20 GMT+10:30.

parameters.name: operation
parameters.description: This parameter searches for the operation field and returns all available results that match. You can use this parameter multiple times and it will do an 'AND' search. You can use * as a wildcard. You can use brackets and a comma to perform an ‘OR’ search e.g [a,b*] will search for ‘a’ OR a value starting with ‘b’.

parameters.name: rid
parameters.description:
This is the unique Request Id for the current request generated by the menu management api. It can be used by H&L to trace requests made on this api.
This parameter searches for the rid field and returns all available results that match. You can use this parameter multiple times and it will do an 'AND' search. You can use * as a wildcard. You can use brackets and a comma to perform an ‘OR’ search e.g [a,b*] will search for ‘a’ OR a value starting with ‘b’.

parameters.description:
The date that the promotion starts.

parameters.name: discountItemsPercentValue

You can use this parameter multiple times. eg discountItemsPercentValue=>5& discountItemsPercentValue=<10 would search for all discountItemsPercentValues between 5 and 10.

parameters.name: discountItemsAmountValue

You can use [1,2,3] to search for discountItemsAmountValues that match either 1, 2 or 3. parameters.description:

You can use [1,2,3] to search for giveawayProductIds that match either 1, 2 or 3. You can use this parameter multiple times. eg giveawayProductId=>5& giveawayProductId=<10 would search for all giveawayProductIds between 5 and 10.

parameters.name: discountAttributionProductId
parameters.description:
If set the total of all discounts are written to this product as a negative value when recording a sale and won't be attributed to individual items.

You can use [1,2,3] to search for discountAttributionProductIds that match either 1, 2 or 3. You can use this parameter multiple times. eg discountAttributionProductId=>5& discountAttributionProductId=<10 would search for all discountAttributionProductIds between 5 and 10.

parameters.name: membersOnly
parameters.description:
Determines if the promotion only available to members.
boolean:

parameters.name: availableAllLocations
parameters.description:
If this is set to true it is available to all locations, otherwise lookup the available locations in MixAndMatchLocations.
boolean:

parameters.name: itemsOnSpecialBehaviour
parameters.description:
Specifies how to deal with items already on special. 'do not include' will not include the discounted item in the mix and match promotion. 'include' will allow the items to be included with all discount rules applied. 'include_no_further_discount' will not apply any further discounts to the items.
This parameter searches for the itemsOnSpecialBehaviour field and returns all available results that match. You can use this parameter multiple times and it will do an 'AND' search. You can use * as a wildcard. You can use brackets and a comma to perform an ‘OR’ search e.g [a,b*] will search for ‘a’ OR a value starting with ‘b’.

parameters.name: posWarningBehaviour
parameters.description:
When applying a mix and match promotion, this setting determines how the pos should behave. If 'prompt user' the user will have the option of applying the promotion. If 'auto apply with warn' the promotion will be applied, but the user will be warned. If 'auto apply no warn' the promotion will be applied without warning.

parameters.name: promotionType
parameters.description:
The type of promotion. 'type' means the offer is issued on a 'transaction' or sale. 'Buy x over x' is designed for offers like buy 4 coffees in one month and get the 5th free. 'batch issued' is used to generate a batch of offers that can be delivered to customers via printed coupons, email campaigns etc.
This parameter searches for the promotionType field and returns all available results that match. You can use this parameter multiple times and it will do an 'AND' search. You can use * as a wildcard. You can use brackets and a comma to perform an ‘OR’ search e.g [a,b*] will search for ‘a’ OR a value starting with ‘b’.

parameters.name: startDatetime
parameters.description:
When the offer starts to be valid. Start time of the day is 00:00
string: This parameter searches the startDatetime field and returns all available results that match. This is a 'relativeDateTime' field. It is relative to the timezone a user resides in and is not an absolute point in time. You can use [12 jan 2020 5:30:20,12 jan 2020 5:30:20] to search for startDatetimes that match either 12 jan 2020 5:30:20 or 12 jan 2020 5:30:20.

parameters.name: endDatetime

Defines the column settings in the grid view for each template.

You will need to have the following data accesses assigned to your user to use this route: sc_get_reporttemplatecolumnsettings

parameters.name: group
parameters.description:
This parameter is used to group results.
                        The fieldName can be any of the following: reportTemplateId.
                        The sort could either have - to sort by descending and + to sort by ascending. See groupQuery schema for more info.
                        For grouping using a nested field use <object>.<field> to specify the nested levels eg +Stock.name

parameters.name: groupSummary
parameters.description:
This parameter is used to summarise grouped results by aggregating the groups.
                The fieldName can be any of the following: templateColumnSettingId, reportTemplateId, columnOrder, groupOrder, sortOrder.
                        The type could be count,min,max,sum,avg. See groupSummaryQuery schema for more info.

parameters.name: totalSummary
parameters.description:
This parameter is used to summarise all grouped results by aggregating all the groups sub groups.
                The fieldName can be any of the following: templateColumnSettingId, reportTemplateId, columnOrder, groupOrder, sortOrder.
                        The type could be count,min,max,sum,avg. See groupSummaryQuery schema for more info.

parameters.name: searchDistinct
parameters.description:
This parameter is used to get the distinct values for a field. 
                Only the field specified will be returned in the results. This can be used with filtering functionality, sort and limit. 
                However it cannot be used with group, groupSummary or totalSummary.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
This parameter is used to change the sorting of results returned. 
                        The default sort is templateColumnSettingId ascending. 
                        Use any fieldNames comma separated in the sort. 
                        Use + for ascending - for descending 
                        eg +updateDateTime.
                        - templateColumnSettingId would sort by updateDateTime ascending and then templateColumnSettingId descending.
 For sorting using a nested field use <object>.<field> to specify the nested levels eg +Stock.name
                        For sorting using a nested field use <object>.<field> to specify the nested levels eg +Stock.name

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: This limits the amount of results returned. This default limit Is set to 20. The maximum limit is 200.

parameters.name: templateColumnSettingId
parameters.description:
Primary Key for the column setting entry.
integer: This parameter searches the templateColumnSettingId field and returns all available results that match. You can use >10 to search for all templateColumnSettingIds greater than 10. You can use [1,2,3] to search for templateColumnSettingIds that match either 1, 2 or 3. You can use this parameter multiple times. eg templateColumnSettingId=>5& templateColumnSettingId=<10 would search for all templateColumnSettingIds between 5 and 10.

parameters.name: reportTemplateId
parameters.description:
Foreign key to ReportTemplates table. Unique with column_name.
integer: This parameter searches the reportTemplateId field and returns all available results that match. You can use >10 to search for all reportTemplateIds greater than 10. You can use [1,2,3] to search for reportTemplateIds that match either 1, 2 or 3. You can use this parameter multiple times. eg reportTemplateId=>5& reportTemplateId=<10 would search for all reportTemplateIds between 5 and 10.

parameters.name: columnName
parameters.description:
Name of the column in the report.
This parameter searches for the columnName field and returns all available results that match. You can use this parameter multiple times and it will do an 'AND' search. You can use * as a wildcard. You can use brackets and a comma to perform an ‘OR’ search e.g [a,b*] will search for ‘a’ OR a value starting with ‘b’.

parameters.name: isVisible
parameters.description:
TRUE if the column is visible in this template.
boolean:

parameters.name: columnOrder
parameters.description:

integer: This parameter searches the columnOrder field and returns all available results that match. You can use >10 to search for all columnOrders greater than 10. You can use [1,2,3] to search for columnOrders that match either 1, 2 or 3. You can use this parameter multiple times. eg columnOrder=>5& columnOrder=<10 would search for all columnOrders between 5 and 10.

parameters.name: isGrouped
parameters.description:
TRUE if the grid should group by this column. Default: FALSE
boolean:

parameters.name: groupOrder
parameters.description:
Order in which this column is grouped (if grouped by multiple columns).
integer: This parameter searches the groupOrder field and returns all available results that match. You can use >10 to search for all groupOrders greater than 10. You can use [1,2,3] to search for groupOrders that match either 1, 2 or 3. You can use this parameter multiple times. eg groupOrder=>5& groupOrder=<10 would search for all groupOrders between 5 and 10.

parameters.name: sortDirection
parameters.description:
Sort direction for this column, e.g., 'ASC' for ascending, 'DESC' for descending.
This parameter searches for the sortDirection field and returns all available results that match. You can use this parameter multiple times and it will do an 'AND' search. You can use * as a wildcard. You can use brackets and a comma to perform an ‘OR’ search e.g [a,b*] will search for ‘a’ OR a value starting with ‘b’.

parameters.name: sortOrder
parameters.description:

integer: This parameter searches the sortOrder field and returns all available results that match. You can use >10 to search for all sortOrders greater than 10. You can use [1,2,3] to search for sortOrders that match either 1, 2 or 3. You can use this parameter multiple times. eg sortOrder=>5& sortOrder=<10 would search for all sortOrders between 5 and 10.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description:
This parameter is used to group results.
                        The fieldName can be any of the following: venueRefId.
                        The sort could either have - to sort by descending and + to sort by ascending. See groupQuery schema for more info.
                        For grouping using a nested field use <object>.<field> to specify the nested levels eg +Stock.name

parameters.name: groupSummary
parameters.description:
This parameter is used to summarise grouped results by aggregating the groups.
                The fieldName can be any of the following: stockAdjustmentId, stockId, locationId, quantity, adjustmentValue, venueRefId.
                        The type could be count,min,max,sum,avg. See groupSummaryQuery schema for more info.

parameters.name: totalSummary
parameters.description:
This parameter is used to summarise all grouped results by aggregating all the groups sub groups.
                The fieldName can be any of the following: stockAdjustmentId, stockId, locationId, quantity, adjustmentValue, venueRefId.
                        The type could be count,min,max,sum,avg. See groupSummaryQuery schema for more info.

parameters.name: searchDistinct
parameters.description:
This parameter is used to get the distinct values for a field. 
                Only the field specified will be returned in the results. This can be used with filtering functionality, sort and limit. 
                However it cannot be used with group, groupSummary or totalSummary.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
This parameter is used to change the sorting of results returned. 
                        The default sort is stockAdjustmentId ascending. 
                        Use any fieldNames comma separated in the sort. 
                        Use + for ascending - for descending

offerId.description: The unique identifier of this record.

description.description: A description of the Offer

promotionType.description: The type of promotion. 'type' means the offer is issued on a 'transaction' or sale. 'Buy x over x' is designed for offers like buy 4 coffees in one month and get the 5th free. 'batch issued' is used to generate a batch of offers that can be delivered to customers via printed coupons, email campaigns etc.

giveawayType.description: The type of giveaway, either a voucher or instant.

startDatetime.description:
When the offer starts to be valid. Start time of the day is 00:00
 This 'startDatetime' field is relative to the timezone a user resides in and is not an absolute point in time.

endDatetime.description:
When the offer finishes. End time of the day is 23:59
 This 'endDatetime' field is relative to the timezone a user resides in and is not an absolute point in time.

redeemStartDatetime.description:
The start date that an offer can be redeemed.
 This 'redeemStartDatetime' field is relative to the timezone a user resides in and is not an absolute point in time.

redeemNumberValidDays.description: The number of days from the date of issue that an offer can be redeemed.

allowExpiryAfterEndDate.description: This allows recipients of a voucher to redeem an offer after the offer end datetime. The redeem valid from and the redeem number valid days will still determine the expiry date.

totalOffersAvailable.description: The maximum number of times the offer can be issued.

offersAvailablePerDay.description: The maximum number of times the offer can be issued per day.

totalOffersReservedForMembers.description: The number of offers issued that are reserved for members. This must be less or equal to the available count.

offersReservedForMembersPerDay.description: The total number of offers issued that are reserved daily for members.

maximumDiscount.description: The maxium discount in dollars that the redeemer can receive.

issuingRequiredSpendAmount.description: The amount that must be spent by a voucher recipient in order to qualify to receive an offer.

issuingRequiredSpendPeriodCount.description: The number of period types the required spend must occure within. Must be set to 1 if the period is 'per transaction' or 'daily'

issueToMembersOnly.description: Whether the offer is only available to members

issueOnRedemption.description: Is this offer issueable on redemption of another voucher.

issuedPerTransaction.description: Determines whether a voucher is issued for each qualifying item in a qualifying transaction that the recipient purchases.

redeemRequiredSpend.description: The amount that must be spent while redeeming to reedem a voucher generated by this offer.

redeemOnceOnly.description: Determines whether a voucher can be redeemed more than once.

redeemOtherDiscountsBehaviour.description: When redeeming, determines how other discounts are treated on the sale. 'no further discount' means that no further discounts can be applied. 'overrides other discount' means that other discounts are overrided with this discount. 'further discounts' means that this offer can be redeemed with other discounts.

redeemByMembersOnly.description: Whether the offer is only redeemable by members

issueScheduledRecurringRule.description: Setup a scheduled recurring rule for when offer is issued.

issueDurationSeconds.description: Used inconjunction with issue schedule recurring rule. When a the recurring rule triggers this field indicates how many seconds the rule is available for.

redemptionScheduledRecurringRule.description: Setup a scheduled recurring rule for when offer can be redeemed.

redemptionDurationSeconds.description: Used inconjunction with redemption scheduled recurring rule. When a the recurring rule triggers this field indicates how many seconds the rule is available for.

barcodeType.description: The type of barcode that is generated when an offer  is issued.

layout.description: The layout of a the receipt

imageUrl.description: An image you want to print out with this voucher

image2Url.description: An image you want to print out with this voucher

discountProductId.description: A reference to the primary key in the Products Table

issuingRequiredSpendPeriod.description: The period type in which the required spend must occur in order to receive an offer

ruleType.description: The type of rule. 'issuing' describes the rules that apply when issuing an offer. 'redemption' describes the products that must be bought when redeeming an offer. 'giveaway' describes which products can be givenaway or discounted.

description.description: The description of the rule e.g Buy 2 bottles of wine.

quantity.description: For a rule type of 'issuing' or 'redeeming' the quantity is the quantity required to be purchased. For a rule type of 'giveaway' it describes the maximum quantity that can be given away or discounted.

discountPercent.description: The discount percent they will receive. Has minumum of 0 and a maximum of 100. Only used for rule type 'giveaway', otherwise should be null.

discountAmount.description: The discount amount they will recieve. Only used for rule type 'giveaway', otherwise should be null.

sellUnitPrice.description: The unit price the customer will pay for the products they receive.

minimumSpend.description: The minimum spend in order to receive this giveway rule. Only used for rule type 'giveaway', otherwise should be null.

mixAndMatchId.description: The unique identifier of this record.

startDate.description:
The date that the promotion starts.
 This 'startDate' field is relative to the timezone a user resides in and is not an absolute point in time.

endDate.description:
The date that the promotion ends.
 This 'endDate' field is relative to the timezone a user resides in and is not an absolute point in time.

totalPrice.description: The total price of the promotion. You can choose to use totalPrice or itemsPriceLevel.

itemsPriceLevel.description: The price level to use for items in the promotion. The promotion price will be calculated using the sum of the items at the price level chosen. You can choose to use itemsPriceLevel or totalPrice.

discountItemsPercentValue.description: The discount percentage value is only used when using items price level. The discount percentage is applied to each item.

discountItemsAmountValue.description: The discount items amount value is only used when using items price level. The discount is evenly shared between the items purchased.

giveawayProductId.description: This is the id of product that is given away with this promotion. The sale price would be recorded as $0.

discountAttributionProductId.description: If set the total of all discounts are written to this product as a negative value when recording a sale and won't be attributed to individual items.

membersOnly.description: Determines if the promotion only available to members.

availableAllLocations.description: If this is set to true it is available to all locations, otherwise lookup the available locations in MixAndMatchLocations.

itemsOnSpecialBehaviour.description: Specifies how to deal with items already on special. 'do not include' will not include the discounted item in the mix and match promotion. 'include' will allow the items to be included with all discount rules applied. 'include_no_further_discount' will not apply any further discounts to the items.

posWarningBehaviour.description: When applying a mix and match promotion, this setting determines how the pos should behave. If 'prompt user' the user will have the option of applying the promotion. If 'auto apply with warn' the promotion will be applied, but the user will be warned. If 'auto apply no warn' the promotion will be applied without warning.

allowFurtherDiscountsAtPos.description: Determines whether further discounting is allowed on this promotion.

singleUsePerSale.description: Determines whether this promotion can only be used once per sale or if it can be used multiple times in one sale.

search.name: search
search.description:
This does an advanced search using a url encoded JSON object.

Most fields available in the return object can be searched using this methodology.
Example: search={ "status": "active"} would search the status field for the value: 'active'.

Searching is also possible using nested fields. Use the following syntax: <object>.<field> to specify the nested field.
Example: search={ "Stock.name": "Best Beer" }

There are a couple of extra operators that can be used in the search. These are $or, $and, $not.
Example: search={ "$or": [ { "status": "bad" }, { "status": "worse" } ] }. Searches for the statuses of 'bad' or 'worse'.
The $or, $and and $not operators can be nested.

If the name pair contains a fieldName it is possible for the value to be a sub-object containing any number of operators. The operators depend on the fieldType of the fieldName:

Date time Allowed Operators: $eq, $ne, $is, $gt, $gte, $lt, $lte, $in
Example: search={ "startTime": { "$gt": "2 November 2021" } }

Relative Date time Allowed Operators: $eq, $ne, $is, $gt, $gte, $lt, $lte, $in
Example: search={ "startTime": { "$gt": "2 November 2021" } }
This 'relativeDateTime' field is relative to the timezone a user resides in and is not an absolute point in time

Number Allowed Operators: $eq, $ne, $is, $not, $or, $gt, $gte, $lt, $lte, $between, $notBetween, $in, $notIn
Example: search={ "totalCount": { "$gt": 10 } }

String Allowed Operators: $eq, $ne, $is, $not, $or, $in, $like, $iLike, $notLike, $notILike, $notIn
Example: search={ "failReason": { "$in": ["Out of bounds", "Out of time"] } }

These operators equate to Sequelize operators. See Operators | Sequelize
